liquid.survey: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Survey of Income and Housing 2019-20 (Household Income and Wealth, Australia)

note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026), Australia, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahwealj992) and average post-tax disposable income (adiincj992) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in AUD of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Savings (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30: only what a family holds as deposits and cash): ABS, Household Income and Wealth, Australia, 2019-20 financial year (released 28 April 2022; the 2023-24 survey released no outputs, the release page says), data cube 7 "Net worth quintiles", Table 7.2 Household assets and liabilities, estimates in $'000, mean per household: value of accounts held with financial institutions (excluding offset accounts), value of offset accounts (deposits held against a mortgage, listed apart), mean net worth and total assets. Times 1000 here. The workbook was read with openpyxl and Table 7.2 saved as CSV. No top 1 percent. Offset accounts are liquid in practice; the lead decides whether to count them.
